name: Dubai
title: Family holidays in Dubai
intro: Winter sun, water parks and the tallest building in the world. Here's what Dubai is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 3 to 4 hrs ahead of the UK

facts.label: Plugs
facts.value: Type G · same as the UK

facts_note: Rules on medicines are strict. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: November to March is the season, with warm sunny days that suit beaches and outdoor sights. Summer is extremely hot, so everything moves indoors, but hotels are much cheaper. Ramadan moves each year and brings shorter opening hours, so check the dates.

things.name: Burj Khalifa
things.blurb: The world's tallest building. Go up near sunset and book ahead.

things.name: Dubai Aquarium
things.blurb: A huge tank inside Dubai Mall that you can see for free.

things.name: Aquaventure Waterpark
things.blurb: Record-breaking slides at Atlantis on the Palm.

things.name: Abra across Dubai Creek
things.blurb: A dirham each. Hop on a wooden water taxi to the old souks.

things.name: Desert safari
things.blurb: Dune drives, camel rides and dinner under the stars. Pick a family-friendly tour.

things.name: Kite Beach
things.blurb: A clean public beach with play areas and a view of the Burj Al Arab.

faqs.question: Is Dubai good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially for winter sun. Hotels are built for families, it's very safe, and the flight is about seven hours with little jet lag.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Five to seven nights mixes beach days with the big sights. It also works well as a stopover on the way to Asia or Australia.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders get a free visit visa on arrival. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: What should we wear?
faqs.answer: Beachwear is fine at the beach and pool. Cover shoulders and knees in malls, the old town and religious sites.
